evidence.evidence_quote: In simulation, adding semantic and BEV supervision increases success rates over a reconstruction-only baseline by an average of 32.03 and 23.73 percentage points (pp) in procedurally generated training and out-of-distribution realistic test environments, respectively. Zero-shot real-world deployments on a Unitree B2-W quadruped demonstrate robust navigation through dense crowds, low-light settings, and construction zones where limited-field-of-view depth policies struggle.

institution_matches.title: End-to-End Reinforcement Learning for Quadrupedal Jumping in Lunar Gravity
institution_matches.overview: The authors present a multistage reinforcement-learning approach that yields a single end-to-end policy for commanded point-to-point jumping in lunar gravity using only mission-compatible onboard sensing. The authors report that in simulation the learned policy achieves accurate point-to-point jumps with landing errors smaller than the robot's body size and maintains performance under control-update freezes of up to 1 s, and that hardware transfer demonstrates successful vertical jumping under lunar-gravity offloading with torque and power profiles consistent with simulation and within hardware limits.

evidence.claim: The authors present a multistage reinforcement-learning approach that yields a single end-to-end policy for commanded point-to-point jumping in lunar gravity using only mission-compatible onboard sensing.
evidence.evidence_quote: We present a multistage reinforcement-learning approach that produces a single end-to-end control policy for commanded point-to-point jumping under lunar gravity. The resulting policy has a simple architecture and relies exclusively on mission-compatible onboard sensing, making its deployment on a real lunar mission plausible.

evidence.claim: The authors report that in simulation the learned policy achieves accurate point-to-point jumps with landing errors smaller than the robot's body size and maintains performance under control-update freezes of up to 1 s, and that hardware transfer demonstrates successful vertical jumping under lunar-gravity offloading with torque and power profiles consistent with simulation and within hardware limits.
evidence.evidence_quote: In simulation, the learned policy performs accurate point-to-point jumps with landing errors smaller than the robot's body size. We analyze the torque and power demands of lunar jumping and characterize performance degradation under extreme outlier events, including control-update freezes of up to \SI{1}{s} during flight. Hardware transfer demonstrates that the policy can successfully execute a vertical jump under lunar-gravity offloading. Furthermore, the measured torque and power profiles are consistent with the simulation results and remain within the robot's hardware limits.

institution_matches.title: Watch Your Step: Anticipated Perception for Humanoid Locomotion
institution_matches.overview: The authors propose an anticipated perception scheme for humanoid locomotion in which a lightweight foothold prediction model uses proprioception and velocity commands to predict future footholds, and the elevation map is sampled only in small patches around these predicted footholds before being passed to the policy. The authors report that with this lightweight preprocessing, the locomotion policy reaches a given terrain difficulty in roughly a third of the training iterations compared to using the complete map, outperforms complete-map policies where footholds are sparse and matches an attention-based encoder at several times lower cost, while transferring zero-shot to a Unitree G1 humanoid on diverse real-world terrains.

evidence.claim: The authors propose an anticipated perception scheme for humanoid locomotion in which a lightweight foothold prediction model uses proprioception and velocity commands to predict future footholds, and the elevation map is sampled only in small patches around these predicted footholds before being passed to the policy.
evidence.evidence_quote: We instead remove redundant inputs from the elevation map before the policy sees it. A lightweight foothold prediction model (FPM) predicts future footholds from proprioception and the velocity command alone, and we sample the elevation map only in small patches around these predicted footholds.

evidence.claim: The authors report that with this lightweight preprocessing, the locomotion policy reaches a given terrain difficulty in roughly a third of the training iterations compared to using the complete map, outperforms complete-map policies where footholds are sparse and matches an attention-based encoder at several times lower cost, while transferring zero-shot to a Unitree G1 humanoid on diverse real-world terrains.
evidence.evidence_quote: With the proposed lightweight preprocessing, the policy reaches a given terrain difficulty in roughly a third of the training iterations required with the complete map. It outperforms policies that observe the complete map where footholds are sparse, including in narrow walled corridors, and on unseen terrain, and it matches an attention-based encoder trained at several times the cost. The policy transfers zero-shot to a Unitree G1 humanoid traversing various obstacles, stairs, gaps, and step-downs beyond the training distribution in both indoor and outdoor environments.

institution_matches.title: Agentic World Action Models
institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model that jointly models code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams in a mixture-of-transformers architecture, where a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands.

evidence.claim: The authors introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model that jointly models code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams in a mixture-of-transformers architecture, where a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands.
evidence.evidence_quote: We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this architecture a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands.

institution_matches.title: GGraph: A GPU-Accelerated Library for Graph-Based Robot Deployment and Learning
institution_matches.overview: The authors present GGraph, an open-source GPU-accelerated graph library that supports both ROS 2-based real-robot deployment and vectorized GPU-based policy training, with built-in support for tasks such as 3-D navigation, exploration, and loop-closure integration. The authors report that GGraph enables graph updates in milliseconds for single-robot operation and allows graph-based exploration policies to train across hundreds of parallel robots, reducing wall-clock training time by one order of magnitude in simulation and real-world experiments.

evidence.claim: The authors present GGraph, an open-source GPU-accelerated graph library that supports both ROS 2-based real-robot deployment and vectorized GPU-based policy training, with built-in support for tasks such as 3-D navigation, exploration, and loop-closure integration.
evidence.evidence_quote: We introduce GGraph, an open-source GPU-accelerated graph library for both robot deployment and large-scale learning. GGraph supports real robots through ROS 2 interfaces and vectorized GPU-based policy training, with built-in support for tasks including 3-D navigation, exploration, and loop-closure integration.

evidence.claim: The authors report that GGraph enables graph updates in milliseconds for single-robot operation and allows graph-based exploration policies to train across hundreds of parallel robots, reducing wall-clock training time by one order of magnitude in simulation and real-world experiments.
evidence.evidence_quote: For single-robot operation, GGraph updates graphs in milliseconds. At scale, it enables graph-based exploration policies to train across hundreds of parallel robots, reducing wall-clock training time by one order of magnitude. Across simulation and real-world experiments, these results establish GGraph as a unified graph infrastructure for both large-scale robot learning and deployment.

institution_matches.title: Do Earth-Trained Humanoid Controllers Walk on the Moon? Gravity, Terrain, and Soil Transfer
institution_matches.overview: The authors study gravity, terrain, and soil transfer for humanoid locomotion by training 12 policies on a simulated Unitree G1 under varying gravity, terrain geometry, and ground contact models, including Earth-to-Moon fine-tuning and gravity randomization, and additionally testing a frozen generalist controller (SONIC). The authors report asymmetric gravity transfer in which Earth-trained policies retain 0.64 to 0.75 survival at the Moon on flat rigid ground while Moon-trained and fine-tuned policies cannot stand at Earth and SONIC survives at most 0.10 at the Moon, and find that rough training can raise combined-tile survival from 0.53 to 0.98 at Earth and 0.80 to 0.99 at the Moon. The authors report that a gravity-randomized policy trained on rough 3D RFT terrain achieves seed-mean survival of at least 0.84 at Earth and 0.96 at the Moon on every key test cell up to 20 degrees, and that Moon-trained policies in sampled rollouts of held-out soil models keep most of their rigid-ground progress on lunar regolith with per-seed progress ratios of 0.84 to 1.39, while noting that lunar results are simulation predictions conditional on the contact model and soil stiffness.

evidence.claim: The authors study gravity, terrain, and soil transfer for humanoid locomotion by training 12 policies on a simulated Unitree G1 under varying gravity, terrain geometry, and ground contact models, including Earth-to-Moon fine-tuning and gravity randomization, and additionally testing a frozen generalist controller (SONIC).
evidence.evidence_quote: On a simulated Unitree G1, we train 12 policies with one recipe, varying gravity, terrain geometry, and ground contact (rigid or three-dimensional resistive force theory, 3D RFT), and including Earth-to-Moon fine-tuning and gravity randomization. We test them at both gravities on rigid ground and 3D RFT, and at their training gravity on three held-out soil models. We also test the frozen SONIC, a released generalist humanoid controller, at both gravities on rigid ground only.

evidence.claim: The authors report asymmetric gravity transfer in which Earth-trained policies retain 0.64 to 0.75 survival at the Moon on flat rigid ground while Moon-trained and fine-tuned policies cannot stand at Earth and SONIC survives at most 0.10 at the Moon, and find that rough training can raise combined-tile survival from 0.53 to 0.98 at Earth and 0.80 to 0.99 at the Moon.
evidence.evidence_quote: Gravity transfer is asymmetric. Earth-trained policies keep 0.64 to 0.75 survival at the Moon on flat rigid ground, Moon-trained and fine-tuned policies cannot stand at Earth, and SONIC survives at most 0.10 at the Moon. Rough training lifts combined-tile survival from 0.53 to 0.98 at Earth and 0.80 to 0.99 at the Moon.

evidence.claim: The authors report that a gravity-randomized policy trained on rough 3D RFT terrain achieves seed-mean survival of at least 0.84 at Earth and 0.96 at the Moon on every key test cell up to 20 degrees, and that Moon-trained policies in sampled rollouts of held-out soil models keep most of their rigid-ground progress on lunar regolith with per-seed progress ratios of 0.84 to 1.39, while noting that lunar results are simulation predictions conditional on the contact model and soil stiffness.
evidence.evidence_quote: In the sampled rollouts of the held-out soil models, Moon-trained policies keep most of their rigid-ground progress on lunar regolith at the low G1 foot pressure, with per-seed progress ratios of 0.84 to 1.39 apart from one seed with a short rigid reference. A gravity-randomized policy trained on rough 3D RFT terrain has a seed-mean survival of at least 0.84 at Earth and 0.96 at the Moon on every key test cell up to 20 degrees. Lunar results are simulation predictions conditional on the contact model and soil stiffness.

institution_matches.title: Flexible Language-Guided Representation Editing for Adaptive Robot Behavior
institution_matches.overview: The authors propose FLEX, a Flexible Feature Editing Pipeline that uses language models to iteratively refine a robot’s internal task-feature representation from natural language corrections by adding missing features, generalizing existing specific features, and masking irrelevant features. The authors report that across 2D navigation, 7DoF Franka tabletop manipulation, and a real-world study with naturalistic language corrections, FLEX requires all three operations in interactive scenarios and achieves consistently higher normalized reward than other feature editing approaches while keeping representations compact and transferable.

evidence.claim: The authors propose FLEX, a Flexible Feature Editing Pipeline that uses language models to iteratively refine a robot’s internal task-feature representation from natural language corrections by adding missing features, generalizing existing specific features, and masking irrelevant features.
evidence.evidence_quote: We propose the Flexible Feature Editing Pipeline (FLEX), which uses language models to iteratively refine a robot's internal representation of task features from natural language corrections via three complementary operations: Add missing features, Generalize existing specific features, and Mask irrelevant features.

evidence.claim: The authors report that across 2D navigation, 7DoF Franka tabletop manipulation, and a real-world study with naturalistic language corrections, FLEX requires all three operations in interactive scenarios and achieves consistently higher normalized reward than other feature editing approaches while keeping representations compact and transferable.
evidence.evidence_quote: We evaluate FLEX on 2D navigation scenarios, 7DoF Franka tabletop manipulation tasks, and a real-world study using naturalistic human language corrections and real-robot demonstrations. Comparisons against single-operation and unscaffolded baselines show that all three operations are necessary in interactive scenarios, and that FLEX achieves consistently higher normalized reward compared to other feature editing approaches while maintaining compact, transferable representations.

institution_matches.title: HyperDrone: Simulation-to-Reality Transfer at Millions of Frames per Second
institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce HyperDrone, a quadrotor simulator that combines highly optimized multirotor dynamics with HyperLux, a new GPU ray-tracing engine supporting Nvidia OptiX, Vulkan, Apple Metal, and WebGPU backends, designed for extremely fast high-performance batch rendering. The authors report that HyperLux can render realistic 3D scenes at millions of frames per second on consumer-grade GPUs, and demonstrate HyperDrone’s utility by training a vision-based yaw-control policy purely in simulation and successfully transferring it to an onboard-running real Crazyflie quadrotor with a camera.

evidence.claim: The authors introduce HyperDrone, a quadrotor simulator that combines highly optimized multirotor dynamics with HyperLux, a new GPU ray-tracing engine supporting Nvidia OptiX, Vulkan, Apple Metal, and WebGPU backends, designed for extremely fast high-performance batch rendering.
evidence.evidence_quote: We present HyperDrone, an extremely fast quadrotor simulator focused on high-performance batch rendering that is more than 20x faster than existing state-of-the-art batch quadrotor simulators. HyperDrone combines highly optimized multirotor dynamics with HyperLux, a new ray-tracing engine that supports Nvidia OptiX, Vulkan, Apple Metal and WebGPU backends that takes full advantage of modern ray-tracing hardware, capable of running both components entirely on the GPU.

evidence.claim: The authors report that HyperLux can render realistic 3D scenes at millions of frames per second on consumer-grade GPUs, and demonstrate HyperDrone’s utility by training a vision-based yaw-control policy purely in simulation and successfully transferring it to an onboard-running real Crazyflie quadrotor with a camera.
evidence.evidence_quote: HyperLux renders RGB, depth, semantic/instance segmentation, surface normals and optical flow observations at configurable levels of fidelity, including reflections, realistic lighting, motion blur, anti-aliasing, and Physically Based Rendering (PBR). Even in the highest-fidelity settings, HyperLux achieves millions of Frames Per Second (FPS) on consumer-grade GPUs while rendering realistic 3D scenes. We demonstrate the merits of HyperDrone by training a vision-based yaw-control policy purely in simulation and transferring it to a real small-scale quadrotor (Crazyflie) with a camera, running completely onboard.

institution_matches.title: Plan First, Act Later: Streaming Reasoning for Executable Memory in Robot Control
institution_matches.overview: The authors propose PAL, a hierarchical memory framework for vision-language robot manipulation that maintains a short-term visual buffer, a semantic-event memory, and an executable subtask list generated from streaming visual observations by a high-level VLM and executed by a low-level VLA policy. The authors report that PAL outperforms prior memory-augmented methods on the RoboMME benchmark and on real-world manipulation tasks, achieving higher success rates than FrameSamp-Modul and MemER. The authors report that proactively writing future-relevant subtasks into hierarchical memory improves long-horizon visual reasoning and robot control.

evidence.claim: The authors propose PAL, a hierarchical memory framework for vision-language robot manipulation that maintains a short-term visual buffer, a semantic-event memory, and an executable subtask list generated from streaming visual observations by a high-level VLM and executed by a low-level VLA policy.
evidence.evidence_quote: we propose PAL (\textbf{P}lan first, \textbf{A}ct \textbf{L}ater), a hierarchical memory framework for vision-language robot manipulation. It maintains a short-term visual buffer, a semantic-event memory, and an executable \texttt{subtask\_list}. A high-level vision-language model (VLM) converts streaming visual observations into the \texttt{subtask\_list}. At execution time, the VLM selects the currently relevant subtask from the \texttt{subtask\_list} and passes it to a low-level vision-language-action (VLA) policy.

evidence.claim: The authors report that PAL outperforms prior memory-augmented methods on the RoboMME benchmark and on real-world manipulation tasks, achieving higher success rates than FrameSamp-Modul and MemER.
evidence.evidence_quote: On RoboMME, PAL achieves a \textbf{56.05\%} success rate, outperforming the strongest baseline, FrameSamp-Modul, at 44.51\%. In real-world experiments across four manipulation tasks, \pal{} reaches \textbf{60.83\%} overall success, surpassing MemER (45.00\%) and FrameSamp-Modul (28.33\%).

evidence.claim: The authors report that proactively writing future-relevant subtasks into hierarchical memory improves long-horizon visual reasoning and robot control.
evidence.evidence_quote: These results show that proactively writing future-relevant subtasks into hierarchical memory improves long-horizon visual reasoning and robot control.

institution_matches.title: RoPT: Robust 6DoF Object Pose Tracking in Video
institution_matches.overview: The authors report that RoPT achieves significantly higher tracking survivability under rapid motion on challenging benchmarks and in real-world robotic demonstrations.

evidence.claim: The authors report that RoPT achieves significantly higher tracking survivability under rapid motion on challenging benchmarks and in real-world robotic demonstrations.
evidence.evidence_quote: We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework across challenging benchmarks alongside real-world robotic demonstrations, achieving significantly higher tracking survivability under rapid motion.

institution_matches.title: Real2Sem2Real: 3D Semantic Augmentations for Robot Learning from a Single Human RGB Demonstration
institution_matches.overview: The authors report that policies trained on data generated by Real2Sem2Real from one human video per task match or exceed policies trained on teleoperation across diverse object instances on two real robots and four tasks.

evidence.claim: The authors report that policies trained on data generated by Real2Sem2Real from one human video per task match or exceed policies trained on teleoperation across diverse object instances on two real robots and four tasks.
evidence.evidence_quote: On two real robots and four tasks, we train a vision-language-action policy on data from one human video per task, and policies trained on our data match or exceed policies trained on teleoperation across diverse object instances.

topic_matches.title: Navigation Explainability for Object Avoidance with LLMs for Assistive Robots
topic_matches.overview: The authors present the Context-Aware Navigation Explanation framework, which integrates perceptual context with planned future trajectories to generate natural-language explanations of guide dog–style robot movements for obstacle avoidance and navigation using a large language model. The authors report that indoor evaluations on a Unitree Go2 platform show a strong positive relationship between explanation satisfaction and trust, and that combining obstacle information with future trajectory yields the most effective explanations.

evidence.claim: The authors present the Context-Aware Navigation Explanation framework, which integrates perceptual context with planned future trajectories to generate natural-language explanations of guide dog–style robot movements for obstacle avoidance and navigation using a large language model.
evidence.evidence_quote: To mitigate this challenge, we present the Context-Aware Navigation Explanation framework that explains guide dog movements for obstacle avoidance and navigation using a large language model. This system integrates perceptual context with planned future trajectories to generate natural-language explanations of robot movement.

evidence.claim: The authors report that indoor evaluations on a Unitree Go2 platform show a strong positive relationship between explanation satisfaction and trust, and that combining obstacle information with future trajectory yields the most effective explanations.
evidence.evidence_quote: We deploy the system on a Unitree Go2 platform in indoor navigation scenarios and evaluate how different explanation context configurations affect user trust and explanation satisfaction. Results show a strong positive relationship between explanation satisfaction and trust, and suggest that combining obstacle information with future trajectory leads to the most effective explanations.

topic_matches.title: State-Dependent Objective Coordination for End-to-End Balance and Navigation
topic_matches.overview: The authors propose a lightweight state-dependent objective coordination method for end-to-end reinforcement learning on two-wheeled inverted-pendulum robots, using a pitch-conditioned scalarization coefficient β(s) to balance navigation and attitude stabilization without auxiliary controllers. The authors report that PPO+β(s) attains 98% and 95% success rates with small attitude excursions on fixed and randomly generated high-obstacle-density maps in simulation, and that zero-shot hardware experiments show bounded attitude and consistent obstacle avoidance using only onboard observations.

evidence.claim: The authors propose a lightweight state-dependent objective coordination method for end-to-end reinforcement learning on two-wheeled inverted-pendulum robots, using a pitch-conditioned scalarization coefficient β(s) to balance navigation and attitude stabilization without auxiliary controllers.
evidence.evidence_quote: We propose a lightweight state-dependent objective coordination method for integrated navigation and control. A pitch-conditioned scalarization coefficient $\beta(s)\in[0,1]$ adjusts the relative contributions of balance stabilization and navigation objectives during training, without extra control hierarchies or auxiliary attitude-stabilization controllers, such as proportional-integral-derivative (PID) or linear-quadratic regulator (LQR) controllers.

evidence.claim: The authors report that PPO+β(s) attains 98% and 95% success rates with small attitude excursions on fixed and randomly generated high-obstacle-density maps in simulation, and that zero-shot hardware experiments show bounded attitude and consistent obstacle avoidance using only onboard observations.
evidence.evidence_quote: Comparisons with alternative reward-weighting, constraint, training, and control-structure strategies show that PPO+$\beta(s)$, where PPO denotes proximal policy optimization, achieves 98% and 95% success rates with small attitude excursions on the fixed obstacle map and the randomly generated high-obstacle-density map, respectively. Zero-shot hardware experiments further demonstrate bounded attitude behavior and consistent obstacle avoidance using only onboard observations.

topic_matches.title: Distance Field Driven Reinforcement Learning for Reactive and Robust Collision Avoidance
topic_matches.institution: National Institute of Informatics; Tokyo University of Science; Universidad Carlos III de Madrid; University of Technology Sydney
topic_matches.overview: The authors propose a reinforcement learning framework that integrates the Euclidean Distance Field directly into the observation space to provide continuous geometric cues for stable, reactive collision avoidance with streamlined reward design. The authors report zero-shot transfer of the EDF-based policy from simulation to a 7-DoF real manipulator, with generalization to unseen real environments and robust online avoidance of dynamic obstacles despite training only with randomized static objects.

evidence.claim: The authors propose a reinforcement learning framework that integrates the Euclidean Distance Field directly into the observation space to provide continuous geometric cues for stable, reactive collision avoidance with streamlined reward design.
evidence.evidence_quote: This paper presents an RL framework that integrates the Euclidean Distance Field (EDF) directly into the observation space, providing the agent with continuous geometric cues that support stable and responsive avoidance behaviours. By leveraging the rich spatial information encoded in the EDF, the method enables a streamlined reward formulation that achieves effective obstacle avoidance both with and without Artificial Potential Field guidance.

evidence.claim: The authors report zero-shot transfer of the EDF-based policy from simulation to a 7-DoF real manipulator, with generalization to unseen real environments and robust online avoidance of dynamic obstacles despite training only with randomized static objects.
evidence.evidence_quote: The proposed approach is validated on a 7-DoF redundant manipulator, demonstrating zero-shot transfer from simulation to real hardware. Despite being trained exclusively with randomised static objects, the deployed policy generalizes to previously unseen real environments and exhibits robust online avoidance of dynamic obstacles.

topic_matches.title: Linear Twisting Sidewinding Gaits for Twistable Snake Robot Motion Planning on Complex Terrains
topic_matches.overview: The authors develop a new family of twisting sidewinding gaits for snake robots based on a linear twisting function that distributes workload across the body and reduces peak output power per twist joint under matched turning speed and total output power. The authors report that the new twisting sidewinding gaits enable locomotion on various terrains where the existing rolling vector approach fails and achieve up to 49% higher speed than conventional sidewinding without twisting in real-robot experiments.

evidence.claim: The authors develop a new family of twisting sidewinding gaits for snake robots based on a linear twisting function that distributes workload across the body and reduces peak output power per twist joint under matched turning speed and total output power.
evidence.evidence_quote: With that in mind, this paper develops a new family of twisting sidewinding gaits that distribute the workload over the entire body with our proposed linear twisting function. Under matched turning speed and total output power, our gaits reduce the peak output power of a single twist joint by 42%.

evidence.claim: The authors report that the new twisting sidewinding gaits enable locomotion on various terrains where the existing rolling vector approach fails and achieve up to 49% higher speed than conventional sidewinding without twisting in real-robot experiments.
evidence.evidence_quote: Real-robot experiments show that, with the reduced workload, our new gaits can locomote the robot in various terrains that the existing rolling vector approach cannot. Besides, our new gaits can move up to 49% faster than conventional sidewinding without twisting.

topic_matches.title: Reconstruction-Augmented Visuomotor Pre-Training of 3D-Grounded Bimanual Dexterity from RGB-Only Human Videos
topic_matches.overview: The authors report that SpatialDex, pre-trained on 1M human-video clips and fine-tuned with few robot demonstrations, outperforms state-of-the-art methods on simulated and real-world bimanual dexterous tasks, and that including reconstructed geometry in pre-training improves success over hand-motion-only pre-training.

evidence.claim: The authors report that SpatialDex, pre-trained on 1M human-video clips and fine-tuned with few robot demonstrations, outperforms state-of-the-art methods on simulated and real-world bimanual dexterous tasks, and that including reconstructed geometry in pre-training improves success over hand-motion-only pre-training.
evidence.evidence_quote: Pre-trained on 1M human-video clips and fine-tuned with a small number of robot demonstrations, SpatialDex outperforms the state-of-the-art methods by 16.5 points on nine simulated dexterous tasks across two embodiments and by 38.3 points on six real-world bimanual dexterous tasks. Under a matched comparison, pre-training with reconstructed geometry improves success by 14.2 points over pre-training on hand motion alone.

topic_matches.title: HuMiT: Low-Latency Whole-Body Humanoid Teleoperation via Compact Reference Tracking
topic_matches.institution: Renmin University of China; The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Tsinghua College AI; Tsinghua IIIS; Tsinghua Weiyang College
topic_matches.overview: The authors introduce HuMiT, a whole-body humanoid teleoperation system based on a unified tracking policy that uses only a compact current-frame reference (root height, root velocity, and SE(3) poses of four sparse keypoints) while achieving tracking fidelity competitive with methods requiring dense reference targets and future frames. The authors report that HuMiT attains a communication-to-inference latency of about 20 ms and a median video-based optical flow latency of 65 ms, and validate on a Unitree G1 humanoid with split-second reactive responses and loco-manipulation capabilities.

evidence.claim: The authors introduce HuMiT, a whole-body humanoid teleoperation system based on a unified tracking policy that uses only a compact current-frame reference (root height, root velocity, and SE(3) poses of four sparse keypoints) while achieving tracking fidelity competitive with methods requiring dense reference targets and future frames.
evidence.evidence_quote: In this work, we present HuMiT, a whole-body teleoperation system built on a unified tracking policy that requires only a compact reference target, consisting of root height, root velocity, and the SE(3) poses of four sparse keypoints at the current frame, yet achieves competitive tracking fidelity compared to methods relying on more diverse reference states including complete joint positions, dense body-part transformations, and even future frames.

evidence.claim: The authors report that HuMiT attains a communication-to-inference latency of about 20 ms and a median video-based optical flow latency of 65 ms, and validate on a Unitree G1 humanoid with split-second reactive responses and loco-manipulation capabilities.
evidence.evidence_quote: Experiments show that our policy achieves a communication-to-inference latency of $\sim$20 ms measured between headset streaming and policy output and a video-based optical flow latency of 65 ms (median) across different motion types. We validate the system on a Unitree G1 humanoid, showcasing split-second reactive responses such as catching a tossed ball, as well as coordinated loco-manipulation capabilities.

topic_matches.title: Object- and Task-Aware Active Perception for Safe Navigation of Mobile Manipulators in Semi-Static Environments
topic_matches.institution: Epson Canada Ltd.; Munich Institute for Robotics and Machine Intelligence (MIRMI); Simon Fraser University; Technical University of Munich; University of Toronto; Vector Institute for Artificial Intelligence
topic_matches.overview: The authors propose an active perception framework for high-DoF mobile manipulators that uses an object- and task-aware probabilistic next-best-view formulation integrated into hierarchical-task model predictive control to inspect uncertain or safety-critical regions with the hand camera during navigation. The authors report that real-world tests and additional simulation and real-world sequences show improved map consistency, reduced task-dependent map entropy, lower navigation risk, and responsive behavior to semi-static scene changes compared to passive or non-task-aware baselines.

evidence.claim: The authors propose an active perception framework for high-DoF mobile manipulators that uses an object- and task-aware probabilistic next-best-view formulation integrated into hierarchical-task model predictive control to inspect uncertain or safety-critical regions with the hand camera during navigation.
evidence.evidence_quote: We propose an active perception framework that enables a high degree-of-freedom (DoF) mobile manipulator to inspect uncertain or safety-critical regions with its hand camera during navigation. A probabilistic, object- and task-aware next-best-view (NBV) formulation prioritizes observations near the desired path and around uncertain or potentially changing objects. The perception objective is integrated into hierarchical-task model predictive control (HTMPC), exploiting kinematic redundancy for viewpoint adjustment while preserving the higher priority of base-trajectory tracking.

evidence.claim: The authors report that real-world tests and additional simulation and real-world sequences show improved map consistency, reduced task-dependent map entropy, lower navigation risk, and responsive behavior to semi-static scene changes compared to passive or non-task-aware baselines.
evidence.evidence_quote: Real-world tests show improved map consistency, reduced task-dependent map entropy, and lower navigation risk than passive or non-task-aware baselines. Additional simulation and real-world sequences demonstrate responses to controlled semi-static scene changes.

topic_matches.title: SP-HLM: Sparse-Pose-Driven Motion Generation and Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
topic_matches.institution: Moore Threads; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; The University of Hong Kong
topic_matches.overview: The authors present SP-HLM, a sparse-pose-driven humanoid loco-manipulation framework that uses five task-critical body poses, a learned latent motion prior, and a pipeline of SP-VLA, SP-MGM, a pretrained motion encoder, and SP-GMT to bridge high-level task policies and whole-body control. The authors report that experiments in both simulation and on a real humanoid robot show improved motion tracking, whole-body coordination, and loco-manipulation success over prior methods.

evidence.claim: The authors present SP-HLM, a sparse-pose-driven humanoid loco-manipulation framework that uses five task-critical body poses, a learned latent motion prior, and a pipeline of SP-VLA, SP-MGM, a pretrained motion encoder, and SP-GMT to bridge high-level task policies and whole-body control.
evidence.evidence_quote: We present SP-HLM, a framework built on a sparse-pose-driven interface. The interface combines five task-critical body poses with a learned latent motion prior to represent spatial intent and whole-body coordination in complementary forms. SP-VLA, a vision-language-action model, first predicts task-relevant sparse poses and finger joint positions from multimodal observations and language instructions using asynchronous action-chunk inference. Given these sparse targets, SP-MGM, a motion generation model trained through two-stage distillation, reconstructs coordinated full-body motion in real time. A pretrained motion encoder maps this motion to a compact latent representation. SP-GMT, a general motion tracker, then integrates the explicit sparse targets with this implicit motion prior for whole-body control.

evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments in both simulation and on a real humanoid robot show improved motion tracking, whole-body coordination, and loco-manipulation success over prior methods.

topic_matches.title: Test-Time Motion Steering for Perceptive Humanoid Fall Recovery

A visual diffusion planner learns from executions of this vocabulary to predict motion intent as future body states.

topic_matches.title: CW-WAM: A Structured Contact-Wrench World Action Model for Force-Sensitive Manipulation
topic_matches.overview: The authors introduce CW-WAM, a structured world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench using a unified interaction module, pair-causal attention over motion-wrench dependencies, and a long fixed-length wrench memory, with the predicted wrench chunk serving as a force reference in a slow-fast admittance-controlled system. The authors report that CW-WAM improves contact prediction, substantially increases insertion success rates for square pegs with 1-mm clearance and power adapters compared with WAM without wrench input, and improves lifting-height accuracy across loads. The authors further report that their framework with an admittance controller reduces force-reference RMSE for peg insertion and wiping and achieves smaller force fluctuations during successful execution.

evidence.claim: The authors introduce CW-WAM, a structured world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench using a unified interaction module, pair-causal attention over motion-wrench dependencies, and a long fixed-length wrench memory, with the predicted wrench chunk serving as a force reference in a slow-fast admittance-controlled system.
evidence.evidence_quote: We present CW-WAM, a world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench. Inspired by hybrid motion-force control, it contains a unified interaction module that treats both motion and contact wrench as modeling targets and predicts time-aligned motion-wrench chunks as control references. A pair-causal attention mechanism structures the motion-wrench dependencies, while a long fixed-length wrench memory retains past interaction information. The predicted wrench chunk acts as a force reference for a 20-Hz outer-loop admittance controller within a slow-fast control system that maintains force feedback and smooth motion between model queries.

evidence.claim: The authors report that CW-WAM improves contact prediction, substantially increases insertion success rates for square pegs with 1-mm clearance and power adapters compared with WAM without wrench input, and improves lifting-height accuracy across loads.
evidence.evidence_quote: CW-WAM improves contact prediction and increases the insertion success rate from 25% to 70% for square pegs with 1-mm clearance per side and from 40% to 95% for power adapters, compared with WAM without wrench input. It also improves lifting-height accuracy across different loads.

evidence.claim: The authors further report that their framework with an admittance controller reduces force-reference RMSE for peg insertion and wiping and achieves smaller force fluctuations during successful execution.
evidence.evidence_quote: Our framework with an admittance controller reduces force-reference RMSE from 4.8 to 2.7 N for peg insertion and from 2.0 to 1.3 N for wiping, respectively, with smaller force fluctuations during successful execution.
